title: Coming to Jershon
summary: After Amulek finishes speaking, they withdraw from the multitude and come to the land of Jershon. The rest of the brethren also come to Jershon after preaching to the Zoramites.
characters: those who withdrew from the multitude

explicit_facts.text: After Amulek finished speaking, they withdrew from the multitude and came to the land of Jershon.
The rest of the brethren came to the land of Jershon after preaching to the Zoramites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Travelers move toward Jershon in two distinct arrivals.
unspecified_visual_details: The route, clothing, and appearance of the travelers.

narration.text: Now it came to pass that after Amulek had made an end of these words, they withdrew themselves from the multitude and came over into the land of Jershon.
Yea, and the rest of the brethren, after they had preached the word unto the Zoramites, also came over into the land of Jershon.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The brethren's preaching is reported as preceding their arrival; its content is not supplied.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the content of Amulek's words or the brethren's preaching.
Do not combine the two arrivals into a single simultaneous event.

title: The Zoramites Reject the Words
summary: The more popular part of the Zoramites consult about the preached words, become angry because the words destroy their craft, and refuse to hearken. They then send and gather people throughout the land and consult with them about the spoken words.
characters: The more popular part of the Zoramites
locations: The land, unnamed in these verses

explicit_facts.text: The more popular part of the Zoramites consulted about the preached words, became angry because the words destroyed their craft, and would not hearken.
They sent and gathered people throughout the land and consulted with them about the spoken words.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The more popular part of the Zoramites can be shown together in consultation.
The later consultation can show them with gathered people.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and arrangement of either consultation.

narration.text: And it came to pass that after the more popular part of the Zoramites had consulted together concerning the words which had been preached unto them, they were angry because of the word, for it did destroy their craft; therefore they would not hearken unto the words.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Keep the initial consultation distinct from the later gathering and consultation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent what anyone said during either consultation.
Do not invent motives beyond the stated anger and effect on their craft.

title: Privately Learning the People's Minds
summary: The rulers, priests, and teachers conceal their desires and privately learn the people's minds. Afterward, many people who favor the words spoken by Alma and his brethren are cast out of the land and come to Jershon.
characters: People who favored the words spoken by Alma and his brethren
locations: The land from which the people were cast out

explicit_facts.text: The rulers, priests, and teachers did not let the people know their desires and privately found out the people's minds.
Afterward, many who favored the words spoken by Alma and his brethren were cast out of the land and came to Jershon.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The private inquiry and the later expulsion and arrival are distinct moments.
unspecified_visual_details: How the rulers, priests, and teachers learned the people's views.
How the people were cast out.
The appearance of the people and the lands.

narration.text: Now their rulers and their priests and their teachers did not let the people know concerning their desires; therefore they found out privily the minds of all the people.

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a public vote, a specific interrogation, a method of expulsion, or dialogue.
Do not depict Alma or his brethren as physically present solely because their words are mentioned.

title: Alma and His Brethren Minister
summary: Alma and his brethren ministered to them.

explicit_facts.text: Alma and his brethren ministered to them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma and his brethren are shown with the people to whom they minister.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, recipients' identities, and form of ministry are not specified.

narration.text: And it came to pass that Alma and his brethren did minister unto them.

prohibited_inventions: Do not name the recipients or location or depict a particular sermon, healing, or other specific act of ministry.

title: The Zoramite Ruler’s Demand
summary: The Zoramites are angry with the people of Ammon in Jershon. Their chief ruler sends a demand that the people of Ammon cast out those who came from the Zoramites, and he threatens them. The people of Ammon do not cast them out; they receive and provide for the poor Zoramites who come to them.
characters: Poor Zoramites who came to Jershon

explicit_facts.text: The Zoramites were angry with the people of Ammon in Jershon.
The Zoramite chief ruler sent to the people of Ammon, desiring that they cast out those who had come from the Zoramites, and made many threats.

The people of Ammon did not fear the threats or cast the people out. They received the poor Zoramites, nourished and clothed them, gave them lands for their inheritance, and administered to them according to their wants.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The ruler’s demand and the people of Ammon’s response can be shown as successive moments, not simultaneous action.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the clothing, provisions, and lands.

narration.text: And now the people of Ammon did not fear their words; therefore they did not cast them out, but they did receive all the poor of the Zoramites that came over unto them;

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent spoken words for the ruler or the people of Ammon.
Do not depict the demand and the later acts of provision as occurring at the same time.

title: Preparations for War
summary: The Zoramites become angry with the people of Ammon and stir the Lamanites to anger against them. The Zoramites and Lamanites begin preparing for war against the people of Ammon and the Nephites. The seventeenth year of the reign of the judges ends.

explicit_facts.text: The Zoramites became angry with the people of Ammon and began to mix with the Lamanites, stirring them to anger against the people of Ammon.
The Zoramites and Lamanites began preparations for war against the people of Ammon and the Nephites.
The seventeenth year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi ended.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Members of the Zoramites and Lamanites can be shown together during preparations for war.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, participants’ appearances, and specific preparations are not described.

narration.text: And thus the Zoramites and the Lamanites began to make preparations for war against the people of Ammon, and also against the Nephites.
And thus ended the seventeenth year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The year’s end is a chronological statement, not a separate visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle or invent specific preparations, speeches, or the cause of the Zoramites’ anger.

title: The People of Ammon Move to Melek
summary: The people of Ammon leave Jershon for Melek, giving place in Jershon for the Nephite armies. War commences between the Lamanites and Nephites in the eighteenth year of the reign of the judges.

explicit_facts.text: The people of Ammon departed from Jershon and came to Melek.
They gave place in Jershon for the Nephite armies to contend with the armies of the Lamanites and Zoramites.
War commenced between the Lamanites and Nephites in the eighteenth year of the reign of the judges.
An account of their wars is to be given later.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people of Ammon can be shown traveling from Jershon toward Melek.
Space in Jershon can be shown becoming available for the Nephite armies.
unspecified_visual_details: The route, travelers’ appearance, and armies’ appearance.

narration.text: And the people of Ammon departed out of the land of Jershon, and came over into the land of Melek, and gave place in the land of Jershon for the armies of the Nephites,
and thus commenced a war betwixt the Lamanites and the Nephites, in the eighteenth year of the reign of the judges;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The commencement of war is reported; no battle is narrated in this verse.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unreported battle or invent the promised later account.

title: Return to Zarahemla
summary: Alma, Ammon, their brethren, and Alma's two sons return to the land of Zarahemla.

explicit_facts.text: Alma, Ammon, their brethren, and Alma's two sons returned to the land of Zarahemla.

Many Zoramites were brought to repentance. Those brought to repentance were driven from their land, had lands for their inheritance in Jershon, and took up arms to defend themselves, their wives, their children, and their lands.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The returning group may be shown arriving in Zarahemla.
unspecified_visual_details: The travelers' appearances, clothing, and route are not specified.
The two sons are not named in this verse.

narration.text: bringing many of the Zoramites to repentance; and as many as were brought to repentance were driven out of their land; but they have lands for their inheritance in the land of Jershon, and they have taken up arms to defend themselves, and their wives, and children, and their lands.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Zoramites' displacement and defense are reported context, not part of the return scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the armed Zoramites sharing the return party's location or moment.
Do not assign names to Alma's two sons or depict a divine figure.

title: Alma's Sorrow
summary: Alma is grieved by his people's iniquity, wars, bloodshed, and contentions. Having declared or sent the word among the people in every city, he sees their hearts beginning to harden and their offense at the strictness of the word. He is exceedingly sorrowful.

explicit_facts.text: Alma was grieved by his people's iniquity, wars, bloodshed, and contentions.
Alma had declared the word, or sent it to be declared, among the people in every city.
Alma saw that people's hearts began to harden and that they began to take offense at the strictness of the word; his heart was exceedingly sorrowful.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma may be shown with an expression of sorrow.
unspecified_visual_details: Alma's appearance, surroundings, and physical expression of sorrow.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the wars, bloodshed, or declarations in every city as happening in the same moment as Alma's sorrow.
Do not invent speech or depict hardened hearts literally.

title: The Sons Are Gathered
summary: A father causes his sons to be gathered so that he might give each a separate charge concerning righteousness. The account of his commandments comes from his own record.

explicit_facts.text: A father caused his sons to be gathered together.
He intended to give each son a separate charge concerning righteousness.
The account of his commandments comes from his own record.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The sons can be shown gathered together.
unspecified_visual_details: The father's name, the sons' names and number, the setting, and the record's appearance are not supplied.

narration.text: Therefore, he caused that his sons should be gathered together, that he might give unto them every one his charge, separately, concerning the things pertaining unto righteousness.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse gives the purpose of the gathering but does not narrate the separate charges being delivered.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the father or sons from material outside the supplied verse.
Do not invent or depict the contents or delivery of the separate charges.
